focus.jnote: Oil eased overnight, but the floor is still shaky. Crude fell Monday after President Trump announced Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy ceasefire — halting strikes on each other’s energy infrastructure after a US diesel-supply deal with Moscow — with WTI near ~$90–92 and Brent ~$103–105. Still, the ceasefire may be narrow (refineries only) and Russia had not confirmed it, and fresh Strait-of-Hormuz tanker attacks over the weekend kept Brent above $100. Equity futures firmed modestly as investors braced for big-bank earnings starting Tuesday. The 10Y sits near ~5.24%, just off 24-year highs, and gold slipped toward ~$4,170–4,185. The scanner boarded one bullish Type C breakout — GME (Grade B) — but it’s a same-day breakout that gapped slightly down pre-market, so it’s a validate-hard, small-size name on a RED day.
focus.notdown: GameStop (GME) is the scanner’s single boarded breakout — it tagged a fresh 52-week high area on 1.83x volume driven by heavy insider buying and a Q2 beat. But be honest: it’s a same-day breakout that gapped down ~0.7% pre-market, sitting just below the pivot, and carries a late-October ~$32 warrant-expiration overhang — a meme-stock with a thin single S/R layer. Banks & financials catch a bid ahead of Tuesday’s earnings open, but that’s anticipation, not a past catalyst. Validate hard at 9:35.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, homebuilders, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.24% and a ~82% December-hike probability priced in. Energy names are two-sided today — oil is falling on the Russia–Ukraine truce, so shorting them risks a violent snap-back on any Hormuz escalation or a Russia walk-back. The disciplined answer on a RED day is to sell nothing new unless it’s a validated breakout at reduced size.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~47 sits at the top of MILD and P(≥1% gap) at ~36% is just above the 35% trigger — the gap trigger alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: a still-active Middle East conflict (Hormuz tanker attacks) stacked on a bond market near 5.24% 24-year-high yields and a Russia–Ukraine truce that Moscow hasn’t confirmed is an unscheduled, open-ended tail. The scanner did board one bullish breakout — GME (Grade B) — but it gapped down pre-market and is a thin, meme-driven name. Trade only validated breakouts at reduced size, or stand down and push DTE past the headline window. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: GameStop (GME) is the scanner’s one boarded breakout — it pushed into fresh 52-week-high territory (pivot ~$26.53, week-52 high ~$26.88) on 1.83x the 50-day volume, driven by heavy insider buying (CEO Ryan Cohen added 700K shares) and a Q2 beat. Liquidity passes (OI ~9,379 on the ATM chain, spread $0.12). Three honest cautions (voiced here, not by dropping the row): (1) it’s a same-day breakout still proving itself — size down; (2) pre-market it is trading ~$25.3, a gap down of ~0.7% below Friday’s ~$26.56 close and below the ~$26.53 pivot, so the breakout is NOT confirmed as holding right now; and (3) there’s a late-October ~$32 warrant-expiration overhang plus only 1 S/R layer (sma20 ~$23.87). Next earnings ~Dec 8 is outside a normal DTE. On a RED day with a below-pivot gap, this is strictly 4-VAL-at-9:35 territory — quarter-to-half size at most, and skip entirely if it opens red.
setups.check_note: Bullish 4-VAL at 9:35: need price > $26.56 (gap holding), > today’s open, and in the upper third of range — AND reclaiming the ~$26.53 pivot. Pre-market it’s gapping down ~$25.3, so it currently FAILS check #1; do not enter unless it reclaims the prior close and pivot. Same-day, meme-driven breakout into a RED tape — size down hard; short put at/below the $26.53 pivot.

risks: Russia–Ukraine energy truce head-fake — Trump announced a ceasefire on strikes to energy infrastructure, but Russia had not confirmed it and a White House official said it may cover only oil refineries; Russia reportedly hit the Kharkiv power plant the same day. Any repudiation re-ignites the oil bid. A top thing to watch.

Strait of Hormuz attacks — fresh weekend tanker incidents near Sohar, Oman and in the strait kept Brent above $100. Roughly a fifth of the world’s oil moves through it; any escalation sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

Bond yields & the Fed — the 10Y sits near ~5.24%, just off 24-year highs, with markets pricing an ~82% probability of a December hike. Any renewed yield pop hits REITs, utilities, housing and small caps hardest.

Big-bank earnings Tue 10/13 — JPM, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Citi open Q3 season into a 24-year-high bond market, stacking macro and single-stock risk. Keep every spread clear of its name’s print and short-dated enough to clear the data.
CPI / PPI watch — a hot inflation number stacked on sticky 5.24% yields and an oil market that could re-spike would be the worst-case macro combination for premium-sellers.

For everything else, keep every spread clear of its name’s print and short-dated enough to clear the data.
